answers.statement: The toy pilot tests only whether nested and alternating training differ; identical solutions would undercut W1's mechanism.
Baseline: alternating updates on the same quadratic; CPU only; no data.
Frozen: quadratic instance and step sizes; the planning claim (C2) is out of scope and stays unknown.
Continue only if the solutions differ; this is a precondition, not evidence for C2.
Local registered pilot; the formal planning experiment would be a v3 task once a baseline exists.

payload.hypothesis: On a two-level quadratic instance, nested (solution-dependent) training and alternating two-loss training reach different solutions, so the two readings of multi-level optimisation are distinct problems
payload.falsification: nested and alternating fixed points coincide
